pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Francis Holland Preparatory School
pageCache.text:
Francis Holland Prep is a caring, supportive community that will provide a strong sense of belonging for your daughter during the formative years of her education.
She will feel inspired and valued, and her natural curiosity will be transformed into a love of learning that will last a lifetime.
Get in touch
Francis Holland Preparatory School provides a warm and inspiring environment in which our girls can learn and thrive. It is a unique community that fosters a care and awareness of the needs of others and a desire to make a difference, both in the school and in the wider world. We are committed to instilling happiness, confidence and lifelong curiosity. Girls are encouraged to be fearless, brave and to be prepared to have a go, no matter how great the challenges before them.
In September 2024, we relocated to our new home in an iconic Grade II listed building in the heart of Chelsea, just off the King’s Road.

Vision and Values
Quick Navigation
You might also like…
Our Values
In keeping with our Christian foundation, we value love, humility, compassion, courage, hope and thankfulness.
Our Vision
Shaped by our values we provide:
An inspiring education in a warm, welcoming community where pupils feel truly known, and girls are encouraged to be brave, unearth their natural curiosity, solve problems creatively and develop a lifelong love of learning.
Our Aims
We achieve our vision by fostering:
A love of learning and enquiry The curiosity to discover and uncover A sense of fun and creativity The development of an ever-growing imagination Respect for others in a friendly, supportive and caring atmosphere The ability to reflect on the outside world with empathy The development of teamwork, leadership and communication skills The courage to be brave, have a go, persevere and succeed.
Our Motto
May our daughters become the cornerstones of the temple. Psalm 144

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Francis Holland Prep from the Head
pageCache.text:
Head’s Welcome
Quick Navigation
You might also like…
As Head of Francis Holland Junior School for six years, I have had the privilege of leading a wonderfully happy, friendly and ambitious community of 4 to 11-year-old girls, and I am delighted and excited to further this success now that we have moved to our new home in Chelsea.
Francis Holland Preparatory School cultivates confident girls who are eager to share their latest fascinating discoveries and achievements. They feel a strong sense of belonging to a supportive community, as we know that when girls feel truly known, loved and valued for who they are, they go on to achieve extraordinary things.
Your daughter will thrive on creative, thought-provoking learning from teachers who will unearth her natural curiosity, feeding it with the foundations needed to develop a deep love of learning and an ever-growing imagination. This thirst for knowledge is evident in our girls’ creative writing, philosophical enquiry, environmental understanding, historical exploration and scientific discoveries.
By Year 6, these lively and inquisitive 10-year-olds will already be debating with gusto, reflecting on the world around them with care and empathy and solving problems creatively. They will be emotionally resilient and intellectually prepared for the transition to their next school, heading off with a listening ear, an alert brain and an eager eye as their next big adventure approaches!
Suzy Dixon Head of Francis Holland Preparatory School

History
Quick Navigation
You might also like…
Founded in 1881 by Francis Holland, Canon of Canterbury Cathedral and Chaplain to Queen Victoria and Edward VII, the school was really the brainchild of his wife, Sibylla Holland (née Lyall).
A house was leased at 80 Coleshill Street, later re-named Eaton Terrace, and on March 1st 1881, at 12.15pm the school, subsequently known as Graham Street School, opened its doors. Due to expanding numbers, it re-located to its present site in October of 1884.
As early as 1882 girls were prepared for the Cambridge Local Examinations and in 1884 a kindergarten was introduced for both girls and boys. The school archive still has the application forms for both Laurence Olivier and Tony Benn!
Threatened with closure throughout its history it has not only survived, but gone from strength to strength. Many traditions live on such as the School’s charitable work, the School Birthday on March 1st and the Old Girls’ Society.
In September 2024, Francis Holland Junior School (which was based at Francis Holland School, Sloane Square in Graham Terrace) relocated to 15 Manresa Road, SW3 6NB and became Francis Holland Preparatory School for girls aged 4-11.
History of Chelsea Library and 15 Manresa Road
Our new home is steeped in history and recognised locally as the former Chelsea Library.
The Public Libraries Act of 1850 and subsequent amending legislation permitted local authorities to provide a library service if a majority of local ratepayers voted for it. At Chelsea a brisk campaign initiated by Benjamin William Findon and supported by the local press had seen the acts adopted a month earlier and when the Library Commissioners sought to build an adequate central library the Earl of Cadogan donated the freehold site in Manresa Road together with £350 towards the purchase of technical books.
15 Manresa Road was designed by the architect John McKean Brydon and opened as Chelsea Library in 1890. Chelsea was amongst the earliest libraries to provide a separate room for children. A boys’ room was included in Chelsea Library and opened each evening between 6 and 9pm. In 1905 this became a fully-fledged children’s library with space for homework, while talks and lantern lectures were also given.
During and air-raid on the evening of 26th September 1940 Chelsea Library was badly damaged by fire, the reference library bookstore suffering in particular. Over 2000 books were destroyed and 10,000 badly damaged. Although temporary accommodation was quickly found in the neighbouring Polytechnic building, the reference and children’s libraries did not re-open until 1949 and it was 1951 before the library was fully operational again. The restored Chelsea reference library re-opened on 2nd May 1949.
When Chelsea Library moved to larger premises in Chelsea Old Town Hall on the King’s Road in 1978, the building (which was Grade II listed in 1969), was taken over by Chelsea College and became the Chelsea College Library. In 1985 the college merged with nearby Queen Elizabeth College and soon thereafter the merged college was itself amalgamated into King’s College London. The building was vacated by King’s College London in 1999.
In 2009 it housed The Hampshire School Chelsea, which was founded in 1928 by visionary artist and teacher, June Hampshire, and started as a dance school. After serving in the WAAF in World War II, her renowned dance school expanded to include an academic curriculum prior to moving to 15 Manresa Road. The Hampshire School Chelsea subsequently closed in July 2024 prior to the opening of Francis Holland Preparatory School in the same building in September 2024.
This magnificent building is now home to Francis Holland Preparatory School offering outstanding education for girls aged 4-11.

ISI Inspection Reports
Quick Navigation
You might also like…
We were inspected in June 2025 and Francis Holland Preparatory School met the standards in every area*.
It is particularly pleasing to see that the ISI inspectors recognised the positive and safe pupil environment that we have at FHS. Inspectors found that ‘reflective leaders ensure that pupils’ wellbeing sits at the heart of their decision making’. The report also highlights that:
*The Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) has a new inspection framework, and this means that both the process of inspections as well as the wording and language style of the report have changed significantly from ISI inspections carried out before Summer 2023. Schools no longer receive overall judgements such as ‘excellent’; instead, the inspectors report on whether a school meets expected ISI standards in five key areas.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Arts - Francis Holland Prep School
pageCache.text:
The Arts
Quick Navigation
You might also like…
Pupils at Francis Holland Prep are encouraged to explore their creativity through the Arts. They participate in a variety of choirs, ensembles, orchestras, theatre performances and art exhibitions. We believe that studying the Arts strengthens girls’ self-confidence, self-discipline and self-expression.
Drama
Drama is a vibrant aspect of life at Francis Holland Prep. Girls from Years 2 – 6 enjoy drama lessons on a weekly basis as well as abundant opportunities outside of lessons, such as Speech and Drama. Throughout the year there are numerous occasions for the girls to perform on stage and showcase their skills, with our big summer musical performance for Years 3 – 6 and the wonderful Nativity for Reception – Year 2. All of our productions are performed in our spacious School Hall with specialist staging and backstage space. Past productions have included: Seussical, Matilda, Oliver!, Mary Poppins, Aladdin and Joseph and His Technicolor Dreamcoat.
Girls learn empathy and emotional intelligence through Drama whilst developing skills such as creativity, collaboration, and confidence, which will support them in all areas of their learning.
Music
Enter the School on any given day of the week and you will find it positively buzzing with the sound of music, whether it be instrumental lessons, choir or ensembles rehearsing. Music is embedded in every girl’s education at Francis Holland as we help all to achieve their musical potential with a vast array of performance opportunities. We deliver hundreds of individual music lessons a week on a diverse array of instruments and the wide range of ensembles on offer produces confident, inquisitive, imaginative and joyful musicians.
Informal concerts give pupils the opportunity to showcase their progress, whether they are new to their instruments or confidently progressing through the grades. We also have a number of show-stopping musical events throughout the year, including concerts, the Fanny Davies Music Festival and the School Musical, all of which take place in our spacious School Hall.
Art
Through a varied and rich curriculum covering drawing, painting, printmaking, textiles and sculpture, art at Francis Holland Prep aims to stimulate creativity and imagination. By creating a safe and nurturing environment, we encourage girls to think outside the box, take creative risks and to learn from the journey, rather than focus on the outcome.
The girls benefit from trips to a wide a variety of galleries and museums in Central London and beyond. We have an ongoing collaboration with The Fashion School with girls taking part in weekly lessons. We invite artists specialising in a variety of fields to deliver workshops, enter the girls into exciting local and national art competitions and provide them with the opportunity to exhibit their work in a fabulous art exhibition!
Ballet
Classical ballet forms part of the curriculum in Reception, Year 1, 2 and 3 and is a popular co-curricular activity from Year 4 upwards. Expertly managed by Chelsea Ballet Schools, the aim of ballet within school is to encourage confidence and to nurture a love of classical ballet, its history, traditions and associate arts. Highly trained teachers provide outstanding tuition for pupils who are prepared for Royal Academy of Dance examinations and continue to achieve a 100% success rate.
A number of exceptionally talented pupils have gone on to attend the Royal Ballet School, both in the Associate Programme and as full time pupils. Francis Holland, Sloane Square offers an 11+ classical ballet scholarship to which Prep School girls consistently apply.

Francis Holland Foresters
Quick Navigation
You might also like…
Our bespoke outdoor education programme takes girls from Year 1 upwards outside the classroom to enjoy the nature around them whilst benefitting from memorable learning opportunities.
Trained by the Wild Passport, our expert staff bring learning to life through teaching bushcraft skills, such as shelter making, den building and fire lighting, using tools, and investigating the surrounding nature. Our outdoor learning follows in-class curriculum objectives to challenge pupils’ learning beyond the classroom.
Girls are encouraged to climb trees and get muddy – the Foresters ethos is rooted in exploration, resilience and connecting with the outdoor environment.

Sport
Quick Navigation
You might also like…
Sport at Francis Holland plays an important part in the life of our school; inspiring, challenging and supporting the potential of our athletes. Our overriding aim is for children to develop skills throughout their time in the Prep School and fondly remember positive experiences which will lead to a life-long love of sport.
We have dedicated outside space and gym facilities for all onsite lessons and fixtures can be played on the netball court at Francis Holland, Sloane Square. We use offsite facilities in Battersea Park for netball, football and athletics lessons for Years 3 – 6, and for swimming lessons we frequent Queen Mother’s Sport Centre in Victoria and Fulham Pools. Above all we offer a supportive environment to allow children to flourish in sport and PE, regardless of age or ability.
Our curriculum covers the following:
We offer a range of inclusive co-curricular sport, and work closely with external coaches in gymnastics, table tennis and tennis to supplement our competitive programme of sporting fixtures with other schools.
Parents are invited to spectate regularly at matches and join us in celebrating our achievements at our annual gymnastics display, open swim sessions, parent fun runs and Sports Day in Battersea Park. Most importantly, our girls are encouraged to participate in an environment where effort, commitment and improvement are rewarded.

pageCache.pageTitle: PSHE Curriculum - Francis Holland Prep School
pageCache.text:
PSHE Curriculum
Quick Navigation
You might also like…
The Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE) programme at Francis Holland Prep is integral to our wellbeing provision, empowering pupils to become healthy, independent, and responsible members of society.
Our weekly specialist lessons follow the six key themes of Being Me in My World, Celebrating Difference, Dreams and Goals, Healthy Me, Relationships and Changing Me. Covering moral, social, and cultural issues that are part of growing up, as well as rights and responsibilities, encourages us to appreciate what it means to be a member of a diverse society. Our girls develop their sense of self-worth by playing a positive role in contributing to school life and the wider community.
Friendology
At Francis Holland Prep, friendship skills are taught explicitly through the dedicated curriculum of ‘Friendology’. Friendology empowers our pupils with the tools and knowledge of how to make good friendships in school and beyond. Girls learn a common language around friendships, how to establish and maintain healthy relationships, manage conflict with kindness and increase their overall resilience. We recognise the importance of fostering these skills in children and therefore dedicate time in every year group to contribute to a culture of kindness, happiness and acceptance at Francis Holland Prep.

Lunch Menu
Quick Navigation

At Francis Holland Prep we strive to provide girls with varied and imaginative menus using a combination of fresh, healthy and seasonal ingredients; aiming to produce delicious dishes which appeal to young people.
Themed and topical menus feature regularly, and menus are produced by committed teams with a real passion for food and service.
